dataset.description:
This Data Management Plan (DMP) is developed for the postdoctoral research project “Enhancing the physico-chemical stability and bioavailability of poorly water-soluble drugs using amorphous solid dispersions” (Project No. 1.1.1.9/LZP/2/25/213) funded under Activity 1.1.1.9 “Post-doctoral Research” of the European Union Cohesion Policy Programme 2021–2027.

The project investigates the formation and properties of amorphous solid dispersions (ASDs) prepared from selected APIs and excipients from different chemical groups. The research combines computational screening, experimental preparation of ASDs using techniques such as co-grinding, solvent evaporation, spray drying and hot-melt extrusion, and advanced characterization methods to understand API–excipient intermolecular interactions and their impact on key physico-chemical properties. The research will generate experimental datasets related to solid-form screening, ASD preparation parameters, structural and spectroscopic characterization (e.g., PXRD, DSC, FTIR, NMR), physico-chemical property measurements (e.g., solubility, dissolution rate, stability testing), and computational modelling results describing intermolecular interactions and molecular structures.

The purpose of this DMP is to ensure that research data generated during the project are properly collected, documented, stored, and shared. Data management will follow FAIR principles (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, and Reusable) and support transparency, reproducibility, and Open Science practices while also considering intellectual property aspects related to potentially patentable pharmaceutical formulations.

distribution.title:
The data will be generated through experimental and computational research aimed at improving the physico-chemical stability and bioavailability of poorly water-soluble active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs) using amorphous solid dispersions (ASDs). The collected data will support the investigation of API–excipient interactions and the evaluation of formulation performance. Experimental datasets will include results from solid-form screening, ASD preparation parameters, and structural and spectroscopic characterization techniques such as PXRD, DSC, FTIR, and NMR. In addition, physico-chemical property measurements—including solubility, dissolution rate, thermal behavior, and stability studies—will be collected. Computational modelling and simulation data describing intermolecular interactions and molecular structure analyses will also be generated.

These datasets will contribute to achieving the project objectives of understanding the role of excipients in stabilizing amorphous forms of APIs and improving their physico-chemical properties. The generated data will support the development of systematic approaches and predictive models for excipient selection in amorphous solid dispersion formulations, thereby contributing to more efficient and cost-effective pharmaceutical formulation development.

dmp.description:
This Data Management Plan (DMP) is developed for the project “ Enhancing the physico-chemical stability and bioavailability of poorly water-soluble drugs using amorphous solid dispersions” (PostDoc No. 1.1.1.9/LZP/2/25/213), funded under Activity 1.1.1.9 “Post-doctoral Research” of the European Union Cohesion Policy Programme 2021–2027.

The project investigates strategies to enhance the physico-chemical stability and bioavailability of poorly water-soluble active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs) through the development and characterization of amorphous solid dispersions (ASDs) formulated with excipients from different chemical groups. The research combines computational screening, experimental preparation of ASDs using various techniques, and advanced structural and physico-chemical characterization to understand how intermolecular interactions between APIs and excipients influence key properties such as physical stability, solubility, dissolution rate, and glass transition behaviour.

The Data Management Plan (DMP) outlines how research data generated during the project, such as computational screening results, experimental formulation parameters, structural characterization data (PXRD, DSC, FTIR, NMR), physico-chemical property measurements (solubility, dissolution profiles, stability studies), and molecular simulation datasets, will be collected, documented, managed, stored, and shared. The DMP ensures that research data are handled according to FAIR principles (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, and Reusable), supports transparency and reproducibility of the research, and promotes Open Science practices while respecting intellectual property considerations related to potentially commercializable amorphous solid dispersion formulations.
